title: Preach until conference, then finish the Bible translation
setting: Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon had preached around Hiram and Kirtland, Ohio, since early December 1831. A later history says their preaching calmed feelings stirred by Ezra Booth’s published letters. They returned to Hiram about 8 January 1832. On 10 January, Joseph dictated this revelation in the John Johnson home, probably with Rigdon as scribe. A general conference was due about two weeks later.
summary: The revelation says the elders should keep preaching in the nearby regions until the conference. At the conference their separate missions will be made known. It then tells Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon to translate again. They should also preach nearby until the conference when it is practical. After that they are to continue translating until the work is finished. This plan is a pattern for the elders until more is revealed. It ends by telling them to gird up their loins and be sober.

contextNote.title: Balancing two assignments
contextNote.text: Joseph and Sidney had laid the Bible revision aside to answer critics. Verse 3 now says it is “expedient to translate again.” Verse 4 keeps preaching in place “inasmuch as it is practicable” until the conference. After the conference, the same verse says translation should continue “until it be finished” as the main task. Verse 2 explains the pause: the conference would assign the elders their missions. In this passage, “expedient” means what fits the present need, and the need had changed.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 71–75 covers this short revelation about balancing duties. How do verses 3–4 divide Joseph and Sidney’s time before and after the conference?
reviewNote: Read all 6 verses. Official heading gives Hiram, 10 January 1832, and the preaching since December. JSP page loaded for the title; full historical introduction read on the Church Historian’s Press study-companion mirror (return about 8 January, Johnson home, conference about two weeks away).
